ESTP>INTJ.title: Someone who goes to look first, then makes a plan.
ESTP>INTJ.body: You head out saying "I'll go take a look," and by the time you're back, you have a plan. Deciding with logic is the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament gets energy from people, looks at what's in front of you, and acts on the spot. Your character thinks alone, looks ahead, and likes to follow a plan.
ESTP>INTJ.say: "I'll go ahead, see how crowded it is, and text you."
ESTP>INTJ.do: You join the gym on the day of your free trial and decide which days you'll go on the way home.
ESTP>INTJ.worry: You want to move right away and you want to plan, both about the same, so you get stuck on when to start. After a day with people, you can't shake off the tiredness without some time alone to think.
ESTP>INTJ.karai: Even at a "today only" sale, you check other stores' prices before you buy.
ESTP>INTJ.aru: When friends invite you, you reply "I'm in!" right away. But the night before, you've planned out the whole day.
ESTP>INTJ.why: By nature, you jump in with people and act on the spot. Along the way, you learned to make plans alone and follow them. That's why, even when you act on a whim, you can get back to the plan in the end.
ESTP>INTJ.yure: Three of the four letters are different, so your result can change a lot. Your answers may split depending on whether you picture yourself on a fun day out or planning at work.
ESTP>INTJ.plus: You get stuck on when to start because you can act fast and plan well. That gives you more ways to go about things.
ESTP>INTJ.tip: When you can't decide, tell yourself, "I'll try it for 30 minutes and check again after." Once you start, the answer shows up faster than if you just think.
ESTP>INTJ.hidden: Your temperament quickly notices small changes right in front of you. It shows when you quickly notice a shop getting crowded or the sky changing color. Use it, and you can act early when plans look like they'll slip.

ESTP>INTP.title: Someone who opens things up to see what's inside.
ESTP>INTP.body: You touch everything first, and while you do, you're thinking, "Why does it work like this?" Thinking with logic and going with the flow are the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament gets energy from people and checks things by touching them. Your character thinks alone and wants to know how things work.
ESTP>INTP.say: "Let's just open it up and look inside."
ESTP>INTP.do: You take apart a broken remote and look up how it works in videos.
ESTP>INTP.worry: You go out as soon as you're invited, but on the way home you're drained from not having enough time alone. Sometimes once you've thought something all the way through, you're satisfied and never actually do it.
ESTP>INTP.karai: You show up right at meeting time and say, "Made it, so it counts."
ESTP>INTP.aru: When you go to an electronics store with friends, you keep trying out the display machines on your own, and your friends move on without you.
ESTP>INTP.why: By nature, you get energy from people and check things by touching them. Along the way, you learned to think through how things work, alone. That's why you get tired when either lively time or quiet thinking time runs short.
ESTP>INTP.yure: Two things are different. You may get stuck on "people or alone time?" and "facts or ideas?", so your result can change. If you answer as your weekend self, the outgoing side is more likely to show up.
ESTP>INTP.plus: You feel satisfied after thinking it through because you can test ideas many times in your head. You're also good with your hands, so just a little more doing will make it real.
ESTP>INTP.tip: Tell a friend about your idea the same day, even in one line. Saying it out loud makes it easier to go "Okay, let's do it," and talking gives you energy too.
ESTP>INTP.hidden: When you buy a new phone, do you have it figured out by the end of the day? That's your temperament's way of checking things with your hands. If you try small versions of your ideas right away, they'll become real much faster.

ESTP>ENTJ.title: Someone who fixes the problem, then plans how to stop it next time.
ESTP>ENTJ.body: When something goes wrong, you're usually the first one moving. Getting energy from people and deciding with logic are the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament looks at what's in front of you and acts on the spot. Your character thinks ahead and plans the steps to reach the goal.
ESTP>ENTJ.say: "Who can move right now? Hands up."
ESTP>ENTJ.do: If the restaurant is full, you call around on the spot and pick the next place.
ESTP>ENTJ.worry: Even with a plan in place, you want to jump at whatever looks fun right now. Some days others seem slow, and you end up pulling too hard on your own.
ESTP>ENTJ.karai: When the elevator's slow, you're already taking the stairs.
ESTP>ENTJ.aru: On the train home from a trip, you're already trying to set the dates for the next one.
ESTP>ENTJ.why: By nature, you react fast to what's in front of you and act on the spot. Along the way, you learned to look ahead and decide the order of things before you move. That's why you can fix a problem on the spot and plan to prevent the next one.
ESTP>ENTJ.yure: Two things are different: "facts or ideas" and "plan or go with the flow." Your result may change depending on whether you picture yourself handling a problem or planning a project.
ESTP>ENTJ.plus: Others seem slow because you can see what's happening now and what's coming. When the team is lost, they turn to you.
ESTP>ENTJ.tip: Before giving directions, ask once, "Where are you stuck right now?" Knowing their pace keeps you from pulling too hard.
ESTP>ENTJ.hidden: In meetings, you're usually the first to spot a small mistake in the numbers. Your temperament sees the facts in front of you clearly. Use it, and people will think, "If the numbers came from you, we're fine."

ESTP>ENTP.title: Someone who comes up with the most ideas in a meeting.
ESTP>ENTP.body: In a discussion, you're usually the one with the most ideas. Getting energy from people, thinking with logic, and going with the flow are the same in your temperament and your character. Only one thing is different: your temperament looks at facts and what happened before, and your character thinks about what no one has tried yet.
ESTP>ENTP.do: When a new game pops into your head while chatting with friends, you start playing it right there.
ESTP>ENTP.worry: You want to try every new idea, so half-finished things pile up. Sometimes you push too hard in a discussion, and things feel a little awkward afterward.
ESTP>ENTP.karai: Anything you start with "I was just thinking…" usually runs long.
ESTP>ENTP.aru: In a meeting, right after saying "Last time we did it like this," you add, "But I want to try something totally different too."
ESTP>ENTP.why: By nature, you value facts and what happened before. Along the way, you learned to think about what no one has tried yet. That's why you can come up with new ideas based on what you've already seen.
ESTP>ENTP.yure: The only difference is "facts or ideas," so you may go back and forth between two types. Answer while thinking about past experience, and you'll lean toward facts. Answer while working on a new project, and you'll lean toward ideas.
ESTP>ENTP.plus: Half-done things pile up because you keep noticing new things to try. Feeling awkward after pushing too hard shows you care about the other person.
ESTP>ENTP.tip: Pick just one idea and try it this week. Once even one becomes real, people will be more willing to go along with your next one.
ESTP>ENTP.hidden: Even with a new sport, does your body get the hang of it before your head does? That's your temperament's way of learning by moving. Use it to make a quick test version of your idea and show people, and they'll get on board more easily.

ESTP>INFJ.title: Someone who thinks for a long time, then suddenly acts one day.
ESTP>INFJ.body: You say yes to plans right away, but once you're home, you slowly think back on the day by yourself. Your temperament and your character are different in all four directions, so some days you act fast, and some days you think things through.
ESTP>INFJ.say: "I think they're having a hard time. I'm going to go see them."
ESTP>INFJ.do: When you notice a friend seems down, you ask "You okay?" on the way home.
ESTP>INFJ.worry: You want to think it through and you want to act now, so some days you feel stuck in between. You pick up on people's feelings so well that you're worn out after seeing them.
ESTP>INFJ.karai: While you're still figuring out what to say to cheer them up, they text you sounding totally fine.
ESTP>INFJ.aru: You spent weeks deciding whether to take a class, then one morning you suddenly signed up and surprised even yourself.
ESTP>INFJ.why: By nature, you get energy from people and act on the spot. Along the way, you learned to take calm time alone and make plans. That's why, after being unsure for a long time, you sometimes suddenly spring into action.
ESTP>INFJ.yure: All four letters are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer as yourself hanging out with friends, or as yourself thinking alone at night, and you might get the opposite result.
ESTP>INFJ.plus: You're tired after seeing people because you really took in how they felt. Lots of people are helped by how quickly you notice and act.
ESTP>INFJ.tip: On days you see people, have a warm drink when you get home and put your phone down for 30 minutes. A little quiet time helps your head settle.
ESTP>INFJ.hidden: Your temperament can stay calm and think with logic. It shows when you're listening to a friend's problem and can already see "what to do first." Use it, and you'll be able to help in real ways, not just listen.

ESTP>INFP.title: You have fun with everyone, then think it over alone.
ESTP>INFP.body: When a friend tells you they're having a hard time, you bring them what they need that same day. Going with the flow is the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament gets energy from people, looks at facts, and decides quickly with logic. Your character thinks about your own feelings alone and chooses based on what matters to you.
ESTP>INFP.say: "I can go now! Where do you want to go?"
ESTP>INFP.do: When you see someone who's lost, you stop to help even if you're in a hurry.
ESTP>INFP.worry: You can act fast, but when you do something that doesn't feel right to you, it hurts later. The more you go along with others to have fun, the more you want time alone.
ESTP>INFP.karai: Right before leaving, you switch outfits "just one more time" and end up a bit late.
ESTP>INFP.aru: You joke around happily with friends, but at home in bed you wonder, "Maybe they didn't like that joke."
ESTP>INFP.why: By nature, you get energy from people and decide quickly with logic. Along the way, you learned to think about your feelings alone. That's why you can act fast and still look back on how you feel afterward.
ESTP>INFP.yure: Three parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Questions like "logic or feelings?" may flip depending on whether you picture work or time with someone you care about. The "go with the flow" side will usually come out the same every time.
ESTP>INFP.plus: You think it over in bed because you're kind. Someone who acts fast and cares afterward is fun and safe to be around.
ESTP>INFP.tip: If something's bugging you, ask lightly the next day, "Hey, about yesterday, you weren't bothered, right?" Once you get an answer, you won't lie awake in bed thinking about it.
ESTP>INFP.hidden: When trouble hits and everyone panics, do you see right away "what we can do now"? That's your temperament's knack for reading the situation fast. Use it, and you can turn your kind feelings into action right away.

ESTP>ENFJ.title: Someone who fires up the team and looks out for each person.
ESTP>ENFJ.body: When a junior teammate messes up, you turn it into a laugh, then quietly show them a tip later. Getting energy from people is the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament looks at facts, decides quickly with logic, and acts on the spot. Your character cares about people's feelings, looks ahead, and makes plans.
ESTP>ENFJ.say: "Not tired? Let's sit down for a bit."
ESTP>ENFJ.do: In a new class, you're the one who starts talking to people you haven't met yet.
ESTP>ENFJ.worry: The more you do for everyone, the more your own wants get pushed back. Even when you'd like to decide fast, you wait for others to feel ready, and decisions get slow.
ESTP>ENFJ.karai: You listen to everyone's problems, but you keep putting off your own worries.
ESTP>ENFJ.aru: In your club you rally everyone with "Let's all go!" and then when you get home, you send each person a "Thanks for today."
ESTP>ENFJ.why: By nature, you look at the facts in front of you and decide quickly with logic. Along the way, you learned to care about people's feelings and support them with an eye on the future. That's why you can lead the group and look out for each person too.
ESTP>ENFJ.yure: Answer as yourself leading the team, and you'll lean toward planning and feelings. Answer as yourself hanging out with friends, and you'll lean toward going with the flow and logic. Three parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Only the "energy from people" side will show up clearly every time.
ESTP>ENFJ.plus: Your own things get pushed back because you pay close attention to everyone. A single word from you puts some people at ease.
ESTP>ENFJ.tip: Before you add other people's plans, put your own things on the calendar first. If they're already there, it's easier to say "I can't that day."
ESTP>ENFJ.hidden: Even when a place is suddenly closed, you can name somewhere else right away: "Okay, let's go to that spot nearby." That's your temperament's way of switching on the spot. You usually make plans, so this hasn't come out much yet. Use it, and you can keep everyone at ease even when things don't go as planned.

ESTP>ENFP.title: Someone who turns "Let's go someday" into a real plan the next day.
ESTP>ENFP.body: When a friend says "I want to try that place," you've gone there together by the end of the week. Getting energy from people and going with the flow are the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament looks at the facts in front of you and decides with logic. Your character gets excited about new things and puts feelings first.
ESTP>ENFP.say: "That sounds fun! I'll book the place."
ESTP>ENFP.do: Even at a party full of strangers, you go up and start talking to people.
ESTP>ENFP.worry: There's so much fun stuff that your schedule and energy are always stretched thin. Even when you want to decide with logic, you picture someone looking let down and hesitate.
ESTP>ENFP.karai: You drop by a get-together "just for a bit" and end up staying till the end.
ESTP>ENFP.aru: On the train home from a trip, you're already talking about the next one.
ESTP>ENFP.why: By nature, you look at the facts in front of you and decide clearly with logic. Along the way, you learned to get excited about new things and care about people's feelings. That's why you can turn "That sounds fun" into a real plan fast, and people can't help joining in.
ESTP>ENFP.yure: The two that tend to change are "facts or ideas" and "logic or feelings." If you answer as yourself planning a fun outing with friends, you're more likely to get a feelings-and-ideas result.
ESTP>ENFP.plus: Your schedule is always tight because you're great at spotting fun things. The places you got everyone to go have become good memories for them.
ESTP>ENFP.tip: Block off one "no plans" day a week on your calendar first. When you turn down an invite, add "I'll invite you next time," and it won't feel awkward.
ESTP>ENFP.hidden: Your temperament can calmly weigh whether something is worth it. It shows when a friend is unsure about a big purchase and you casually ask, "How many times a month would you use it?" Use it, and people will count on you when it matters.

ESTP>ISTJ.title: Usually careful, but quick to act when something comes up.
ESTP>ISTJ.body: People usually see you as neat and careful about rules. But when something unexpected happens, you're the first to move, and that surprises them a little. Looking at facts and deciding with logic are the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament gets energy from people and acts on the spot. Your character likes calm time alone and sticks to the steps.
ESTP>ISTJ.say: "Let's do it the same way as before. That's the safest bet."
ESTP>ISTJ.do: After shopping, you check that the receipt matches the amount in your money app.
ESTP>ISTJ.worry: You like to prepare properly, but when every day is the same, you get restless. After a lively time, you can't settle down until you tidy up alone.
ESTP>ISTJ.karai: You pick restaurants by review scores and how close they are to the station, not the vibe.
ESTP>ISTJ.aru: You feel settled leaving home at the same time and riding the same train car every morning. But after too many days the same, you suddenly want to take a different way home.
ESTP>ISTJ.why: By nature, you get energy from people and act fast on the spot. Along the way, you learned to prepare calmly alone and stick to the steps. That's why you can follow the rules and still improvise when you need to.
ESTP>ISTJ.yure: Two things are different: "people or alone" and "plan or go with the flow." Answer as yourself at work on a weekday, and you'll lean toward a careful type. Answer as yourself on a trip, and you'll lean toward an outgoing type.
ESTP>ISTJ.plus: You get restless with the same old days because you can enjoy change too. People love it when a careful person shows a little playful side.
ESTP>ISTJ.tip: Add a "try a new place" day to your routine once a month. Even a small change like that will ease the restless feeling.
ESTP>ISTJ.hidden: On trips or in waiting rooms, do you find yourself deep in conversation with the person next to you? That's your temperament's way of making friends fast, even with strangers. Show it at work too, and people will find you easy to come to.

ESTP>ISFJ.title: Someone whose hands move first when they see someone in need.
ESTP>ISFJ.body: On group outings, you often look back to check that no one's falling behind. Trusting facts and experience is the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament gets energy from people, decides quickly with logic, and acts on the spot. Your character likes calm time alone, cares about people's feelings, and prepares properly.
ESTP>ISFJ.do: When you see a snack a friend once said they liked, you buy it and give it to them.
ESTP>ISFJ.worry: Because you're so quick to help, favors keep filling up your schedule. Even on days you want to relax, you feel you should be doing something and can't rest.
ESTP>ISFJ.karai: You say you "just eyeball it," but your cooking tastes exactly the same every time.
ESTP>ISFJ.aru: When a friend texts "I think I have a fever," you can't sit still, and you drop off some food that same day.
ESTP>ISFJ.why: By nature, you decide quickly with logic and act right away. Along the way, you learned to care about people's feelings and prepare properly. That's why you can see right away what someone needs, and your hands start moving.
ESTP>ISFJ.yure: Three of the four letters are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer as yourself taking care of others, and you'll lean toward a quiet type who's good at looking after people. The "facts" side will almost always stay the same.
ESTP>ISFJ.plus: Your schedule fills up with favors because your help really makes a difference. If you say no once in a while, people will understand.
ESTP>ISFJ.tip: Each time you say yes to a favor, add one fun plan for yourself too. Keeping "for others" and "for me" even makes it easier to rest.
ESTP>ISFJ.hidden: Your temperament can also decide simply, with logic. It shows when a friend can't decide and you say right away, "This way's faster." Use it for yourself, and you'll pick which favors to take on, and have more free time.

ESTP>ESTJ.title: Someone who acts fast, then sets rules for next time.
ESTP>ESTJ.body: When trouble comes up, you go check it out right away, and once it's fixed, you set a rule: "From now on, let's do it this way." Getting energy from people, looking at facts, and deciding with logic are the same in your temperament and your character. Only one thing is different: your temperament likes to go with the flow, and your character likes to follow the plan exactly.
ESTP>ESTJ.say: "I'll go handle it. Let's rethink how we do it when I'm back."
ESTP>ESTJ.do: You plan the barbecue, and the moment you see rain clouds, you switch to a covered spot.
ESTP>ESTJ.worry: Sometimes you want people to follow the rules, and sometimes you want to just go for it, and switching between the two can wear you out. You worry that moving things along so fast makes you seem "a little scary."
ESTP>ESTJ.karai: When the bill comes, you're the fastest to split it on your phone.
ESTP>ESTJ.aru: You carefully planned the family trip, then changed where you were going on the day because "this looks better," and your family asked, "So what was the plan for?"
ESTP>ESTJ.why: By nature, you like to go with the flow. Along the way, you learned to make plans and follow them properly. That's why you can make rules and change them on the spot too.
ESTP>ESTJ.yure: The only difference is "plan or go with the flow," so you may go back and forth between two types. Answer as yourself before a deadline, and you'll lean toward planning. Answer as yourself on a day off, and you'll lean toward going with the flow.
ESTP>ESTJ.plus: Switching wears you out because you're always trying to pick the best way for the moment. Someone who's good with rules and sudden changes is relied on anywhere.
ESTP>ESTJ.tip: When you make a plan, leave one slot that says "decide on the day." After moving things along fast, add "Sorry for rushing, thanks for the help," and you won't seem so scary.
ESTP>ESTJ.hidden: When you get an unexpected question in a meeting, do you somehow feel a little excited answering it? That's your temperament's way of enjoying surprises. Use it, and you'll be the one people turn to when plans fall apart.

ESTP>ESFJ.title: Someone who often gets asked to plan the get-together.
ESTP>ESFJ.body: By the end of a get-together, you've remembered the names of everyone you just met. Getting energy from people and paying attention to the facts in front of you are the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament decides quickly with logic and acts on the spot. Your character cares about people's feelings and prepares ahead.
ESTP>ESFJ.say: "Let's all go together, it's way more fun."
ESTP>ESFJ.do: At a barbecue, you quickly sort out the shopping and who does what, then spend the rest of the time playing with the kids.
ESTP>ESFJ.worry: Even when you want to say something clearly, you sometimes keep it in because you don't want to spoil the mood. While getting things ready for everyone, you run out of time to enjoy yourself.
ESTP>ESFJ.karai: Someone just asks you for directions, and you end up recommending a good restaurant too.
ESTP>ESFJ.aru: When you plan the party, you handle the orders and the seating, and on the way home you realize, "Wait, I didn't eat anything."
ESTP>ESFJ.why: By nature, you decide quickly with logic and act on the spot. Along the way, you learned to care about how others feel and prepare things for everyone. That's why you can tell right away what's needed and get moving.
ESTP>ESFJ.yure: Two things are different: "logic or feelings" and "plan or go with the flow." Answer as yourself planning a party, and you'll lean toward feelings and planning. Answer as yourself just going along, and you'll lean toward logic and going with the flow.
ESTP>ESFJ.plus: You hold things back because you care about the mood. You're someone who can speak plainly, so with a slightly different way of saying it, you can get your point across without spoiling things.
ESTP>ESFJ.tip: On days you're the organizer, make the first 10 minutes after the toast your "eating time." When you have something to say, start with "Here's one idea," and it'll be easier to say.
ESTP>ESFJ.hidden: Your temperament can make quick, clear decisions. It shows when a discussion drags on and you say, "Okay, let's just vote." Use it, and you can move things along faster while still caring about how everyone feels.

ESTP>ISTP.title: Someone who gets put in charge of the campfire.
ESTP>ISTP.body: You can be chatting away, but when something breaks, you go quiet and start fixing it. Looking at facts, thinking with logic, and going with the flow are the same in your temperament and your character. Only where your energy comes from is different: your temperament gets energy from people, and your character recharges alone.
ESTP>ISTP.say: "Let's all go sometime. I'll scout it out alone first."
ESTP>ISTP.do: When an appliance stops working, you just poke around until it's fixed.
ESTP>ISTP.worry: There's a big gap between days you want people around and days you don't want anyone talking to you, and it confuses others. You can't really explain how your mood changes.
ESTP>ISTP.karai: Get you talking about tools and suddenly you won't stop.
ESTP>ISTP.aru: You planned to go out with friends this weekend, but on Saturday morning you change your mind: "Today I just want to work on my bike alone."
ESTP>ISTP.why: By nature, you get energy from people. Along the way, you learned to recharge by working quietly with your hands alone. That's why, even if your mood seems to change, what you do always makes sense.
ESTP>ISTP.yure: Only one thing is different. Your answer to "Do you get energy from people or from alone time?" can change, so you may go back and forth between two types. Take it on a day you were focused on a project, and you'll lean toward the alone side.
ESTP>ISTP.plus: Your moods swing a lot because you can get energy from lively time and quiet time. You have more ways to recharge than most.
ESTP>ISTP.tip: When you feel "today's an alone day," tell your friends first in one line. You don't need a good explanation. "Recharge day today" is enough.
ESTP>ISTP.hidden: At a get-together after a long time, do you find yourself at the center of the conversation? Your temperament knows how to liven up a group. Use it, and it'll be easier to share what you're good at, and you'll make more friends.

ESTP>ISFP.title: Someone who wanders into a shop and finds a new favorite.
ESTP>ISFP.body: You walk into a shop on a whim, make friends with the staff, and come home with clothes you love. Paying attention to what's in front of you and going with the flow are the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament gets energy from people and decides simply with logic. Your character enjoys favorite things alone and chooses by what you like.
ESTP>ISFP.say: "Let's just go see. If we like something, we can buy it."
ESTP>ISFP.do: When you see a beautiful sunset on a walk, you stop and take a photo.
ESTP>ISFP.worry: Even when you want to decide simply, your likes and dislikes show on your face. After a fun time with people, you can't settle down without some time alone doing what you love.
ESTP>ISFP.karai: You do most things on a whim, but when it comes to clothes and accessories, you won't settle.
ESTP>ISFP.aru: Shopping with friends, you happily go from store to store, but when it comes to picking your own clothes, you suddenly get serious.
ESTP>ISFP.why: By nature, you get energy from people and decide simply with logic. Along the way, you learned to value time alone and choose by what you like. That's why, even when you head out on a whim, you never miss something pretty or something you love.
ESTP>ISFP.yure: Your answers tend to change on "energy from people or alone?" and "logic or feelings?" If you answer as yourself absorbed in a hobby, you're more likely to get an alone-and-feelings result.
ESTP>ISFP.plus: Your likes and dislikes show because you trust how you feel. People probably ask you to "help me pick" a lot.
ESTP>ISFP.tip: On days with fun plans, save "30 minutes alone" for the way home. Just having that will help you enjoy yourself to the end.
ESTP>ISFP.hidden: When choosing an appliance or a phone, can you quickly compare price and specs and decide without much fuss? That's your temperament's way of calmly comparing things. Use it, and it'll be easier to explain to people why you "just like" something.

ESTP>ESTP.title: Someone whose body moves before their head does.
ESTP>ESTP.body: Before you even look up directions on your phone, you've already asked someone nearby. Your temperament and your character point the same way in all four directions, so your knack for reading the moment and acting fast has grown strong. You do great in places full of change, and you get tired for no clear reason in places where you just have to wait.
ESTP>ESTP.say: "No point wasting time deciding. Let's go."
ESTP>ESTP.do: On trips, you skip the detailed plans and decide where to go once you get off the train.
ESTP>ESTP.worry: You put off future stuff and then get a scare with deadlines and paperwork. When boring days keep coming, your energy fades without you knowing why.
ESTP>ESTP.karai: "I'll do it later" usually means the morning it's due.
ESTP>ESTP.aru: When you hear a new shop opened, you're already in line on your way home that day, sending friends a photo: "I went!"
ESTP>ESTP.why: By nature and now, you get energy from people, look at the facts in front of you, decide with logic, and act fast. That's why you get moving really quickly, and long, boring tasks feel hard.
ESTP>ESTP.yure: You'll usually get the same result every time. If a careful or planner type shows up, you may be in a stretch where work wants you to slow down, or you can't move freely and your energy is a little low.
ESTP>ESTP.plus: Paperwork gets pushed back because you act right away on what's in front of you. Thanks to that, you never miss out on the fun.
ESTP>ESTP.tip: Stick a "just 5 minutes" of annoying paperwork right before something fun. In a boring week, even taking a new way home can bring your energy back.
ESTP>ESTP.hidden: You're great at acting fast, but you can also stick with something for a long time. It shows when you spend hours working out the same thing in a game or hobby you love. Use it, and you'll be able to finish the things you started on impulse.

ESTP>ESFP.title: Someone who's always at the center of the fun.
ESTP>ESFP.body: Even while you're keeping the party going, part of you is watching how things are going. Getting energy from people, enjoying the moment, and going with the flow are the same in your temperament and your character. Only one thing is different: your temperament decides quickly with logic, and your character decides by caring about people's feelings.
ESTP>ESFP.do: At a friend's surprise party, you're the most excited one, and you settle the bill split right there too.
ESTP>ESFP.worry: You don't want to ruin the fun, so you often turn things you should say into jokes. After you say something plainly, you worry if you hurt them.
ESTP>ESFP.karai: The person who was most excited is the one going over what went wrong on the way home.
ESTP>ESFP.aru: After telling a friend your honest opinion, you keep rereading the chat at home: "Did that sound harsh?"
ESTP>ESFP.why: By nature, you decide quickly with logic. Along the way, you learned to decide by caring about people's feelings. That's why, even in the middle of the fun, you can make calm decisions and notice how others feel.
ESTP>ESFP.yure: The only difference is "logic or feelings," so you may go back and forth between two types. Answer as yourself deciding money or plans at work, and you'll lean toward logic. Answer as yourself helping a friend with a problem, and you'll lean toward feelings.
ESTP>ESFP.plus: You keep rereading it because you don't want to hurt them. People trust someone who can be honest and caring at the same time.
ESTP>ESFP.tip: After being direct, send a quick "Sorry if that was too much." It makes it easier for them to reply, so you won't need to keep rereading the chat.
ESTP>ESFP.hidden: When planning a trip budget, you may be the fastest to figure out "how much per person." Your temperament is quick with numbers and what's worth it. Use it, and your fun plans are more likely to actually happen.

ESFP>INTJ.title: Someone who plans carefully but never forgets to have fun.
ESFP>INTJ.body: You make plans and stick to them. But you've always loved having fun. When friends get together, you quickly book the place, pick a time to meet, and send it to everyone.
ESFP>INTJ.do: At work, you plan out the whole schedule first, then take it one step at a time.
ESFP>INTJ.worry: On days off, you can't decide whether to follow a plan or go with your mood. After a lively time, if you don't get some quiet time alone, you stay tired.
ESFP>INTJ.karai: Out of the whole plan, the part you're most excited about is the after-party.
ESFP>INTJ.aru: You planned the trip carefully, but on the day you're the first one saying, "Let's go this way!"
ESFP>INTJ.why: By nature, you enjoy the moment and go with the flow. Along the way, you learned to look ahead and stick to a plan. That's why people may see you very differently depending on the situation.
ESFP>INTJ.yure: All four are different, so your result can change completely each time. Depending on whether you picture yourself making plans at work or goofing around with friends, you could get opposite types.
ESFP>INTJ.plus: You're torn because you like being organized and you like having fun. When you make the plan, everyone can relax and enjoy it.
ESFP>INTJ.tip: Put some "do nothing" time into your day-off plans from the start. If things change, you can adjust there, so you won't get annoyed.
ESFP>INTJ.hidden: By nature, you quickly pick up on how people feel. Do you hand a snack to a coworker who looks down before even asking what's wrong? At work too, ask "Are you okay?" first, and the talk goes more smoothly.

ESFP>INTP.title: Even when you're out having fun, you end up thinking about how things work.
ESFP>INTP.body: You were having a blast at the amusement park, and then you catch yourself thinking about how the line moves. Going with the flow is the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament gets energy from people, enjoys the fun in front of you, and puts feelings first. Your character thinks about how things work alone and finds answers with logic.
ESFP>INTP.say: "Hey, why do you think this happens?"
ESFP>INTP.do: When you play board games, you're figuring out how winning works as you play.
ESFP>INTP.worry: You love talking with people, but when you get lost in thought, you forget to reply. Sometimes you answer with logic when you meant to be caring, and you feel bad later.
ESFP>INTP.karai: "That was fun!" tends to get the reply, "The system was so interesting."
ESFP>INTP.aru: On the way home from the aquarium with friends, you start wondering "How do jellyfish swim?" and ignore the group chat to look it up.
ESFP>INTP.why: By nature, you get energy from people and care about others' feelings. Along the way, you learned to think through how things work alone and find answers with logic. That's why, in the middle of a chat, you suddenly notice a "why?"
ESFP>INTP.yure: If you answer as yourself lost in thought, you'll lean toward alone, ideas, and logic. Three parts are different, so your result can change a lot, but the "go with the flow" side will show up clearly every time.
ESFP>INTP.plus: You can get so into something that you forget to reply because you can really focus on one thing. Your "why?" often gets the conversation going.
ESFP>INTP.tip: Before you dive into looking something up, send a quick "Something just caught my interest, I'll reply later." Save what you find out to talk about next time you meet.
ESFP>INTP.hidden: When you're explaining something, you sometimes watch the other person's face and soften how you say it. That's your temperament's way of noticing how people feel. Use it, and your ideas will get across more easily.

ESFP>ENTJ.title: Someone who leads the team and hands out snacks too.
ESFP>ENTJ.body: After setting a clear goal in the meeting, you go around handing out snacks. Getting energy from people is the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament enjoys the moment, decides with feelings, and acts on the spot. Your character thinks ahead, decides with logic, and plans the way to the goal.
ESFP>ENTJ.say: "Let's all get this done by Friday!"
ESFP>ENTJ.do: You plan the office bowling night, right down to team rules and prizes.
ESFP>ENTJ.worry: You want results so much that after being strict, you worry about how the other person feels. Some days your head is so full of plans that you can't enjoy the fun right in front of you.
ESFP>ENTJ.karai: You said you'd go shopping alone, and then you invited a friend anyway.
ESFP>ENTJ.aru: On nights after you've corrected a younger coworker, you can't fall asleep, wondering, "Was I too harsh?"
ESFP>ENTJ.why: By nature, you enjoy the fun in front of you and act on the spot. Along the way, you learned to think about future goals and move through the plan step by step. That's why, even when your goals are high, people happily follow you.
ESFP>ENTJ.yure: Three parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer as yourself chasing goals at work, and you'll lean toward logic, planning, and ideas. Answer as yourself having fun on a day off, and you'll lean toward feelings, going with the flow, and facts.
ESFP>ENTJ.plus: You worry after being strict because you care about how people feel. Not many leaders care about both results and people.
ESFP>ENTJ.tip: When you share a goal, set a reward with it, like "If we hit it, let's all go do something fun." After correcting someone, send a short "I'm counting on you" that same day.
ESFP>ENTJ.hidden: Your temperament knows how to enjoy the moment. It shows when you happily say yes to an unplanned detour or a last-minute invite. You usually follow the plan, so this hasn't come out much yet. Use it, and your team's mood will get even brighter.

ESFP>ENTP.title: A casual chat with you turns into a plan to hang out.
ESFP>ENTP.body: While you're making everyone laugh, a plan for something fun somehow comes together. Getting energy from people and going with the flow are the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament enjoys the moment and cares about people's feelings. Your character comes up with new ideas and puts them together with logic.
ESFP>ENTP.say: "Ooh, that sounds fun! Let's do it now."
ESFP>ENTP.do: You casually said "Let's make takoyaki at my place," and now it's a party with a bunch of friends.
ESFP>ENTP.worry: You jump at every fun idea, so half-done things keep piling up. After getting heated in a discussion, you watch the other person's face, worried you went too far.
ESFP>ENTP.karai: You've said "Let's do that sometime" about way more things than you've actually done.
ESFP>ENTP.aru: You get worked up in a discussion and say things too strongly, then afterward you see their face and suddenly feel bad.
ESFP>ENTP.why: By nature, you feel the fun in front of you and care about people's feelings. Along the way, you learned to come up with new ideas and build them with logic. That's why you can turn a joke into a real plan.
ESFP>ENTP.yure: Answer as yourself brainstorming a plan, and you'll lean toward ideas and logic. Answer as yourself hanging out with friends, and you'll lean toward facts and feelings. Two parts are different, so your result can change.
ESFP>ENTP.plus: Half-done projects pile up because you notice fun things right away. When you look like you're having fun, others want to join in.
ESFP>ENTP.tip: Before starting something new, mark one half-done thing as "done" or "on break." After a discussion, say "I'm glad we talked," and you'll end on a good note.
ESFP>ENTP.hidden: When you eat something delicious, you can describe the taste and smell in detail. That's your temperament's way of really savoring what's in front of you. Use it, and when you talk about ideas, people can picture them more easily.

ESFP>INFJ.title: Someone who notices the lonely-looking person, even in a lively crowd.
ESFP>INFJ.body: On the way home from a day full of laughs, you think back: "Maybe that person was worried about something." Deciding with feelings is the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament gets energy from people, enjoys the moment, and acts on the spot. Your character likes calm time alone, thinks about what others are thinking and what's ahead, and prepares.
ESFP>INFJ.do: When a friend calls sounding down, you go see them right away.
ESFP>INFJ.worry: You love seeing people, but afterward you're more tired than you expected. You think so much about how others feel that you worry about things that haven't even happened.
ESFP>INFJ.karai: You worry about others right away, but don't notice when you're tired yourself.
ESFP>INFJ.aru: In a group photo, when you notice someone off at the edge, you call them to the middle. Back home, you can't sleep, wondering, "Will they be okay tomorrow?"
ESFP>INFJ.why: By nature, you get energy from people and feel the fun in front of you. Along the way, you learned to take calm time alone and think about what people really feel. That's why, even while you're keeping things lively, you notice someone who looks lonely.
ESFP>INFJ.yure: Three parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answer as yourself in a lively crowd, and you'll lean toward going with the flow and facts. Answer as yourself thinking alone at night, and you'll lean toward alone, ideas, and planning. The "feelings" side will show up the same either way.
ESFP>INFJ.plus: You worry about what's ahead because you think about people so much. That's why you notice right away when someone is struggling.
ESFP>INFJ.tip: On nights after seeing people, send "Thanks for today, let me know if anything's up" to anyone you're worried about, then go to bed. Once you've sent it, you can leave the rest to them.
ESFP>INFJ.hidden: Have you ever been at a party full of strangers and suddenly found yourself at the center of the laughs? Your temperament can slip easily into a group. Use it, and even in a new place, it's easier to talk to someone who looks lonely.

ESFP>INFP.title: Someone who looks back at photos from a fun day again and again.
ESFP>INFP.body: On the way home from a fun day with friends, you remember every view you saw. Deciding with feelings and going with the flow are the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament gets energy from people and notices beautiful things in front of you. Your character thinks about your own feelings alone and lets your imagination grow.
ESFP>INFP.say: "How do I even put this feeling into words?"
ESFP>INFP.do: When you buy souvenirs on a trip, you pick a different one for each friend.
ESFP>INFP.worry: Time with friends and time alone daydreaming both matter to you, so you swing between overbooking yourself and hiding at home. You can't put what matters to you into words, and it frustrates you.
ESFP>INFP.karai: If the staff were rude, you never go back, no matter how good the food was.
ESFP>INFP.aru: After a weekend packed with plans, the next week you suddenly want to see no one and just watch your favorite movies in your room.
ESFP>INFP.why: By nature, you get energy from people and enjoy the views and fun in front of you. Along the way, you learned to let your imagination grow alone. That's why it's natural to have weeks when you go out a lot and weeks when you want to stay home.
ESFP>INFP.yure: Two parts are different, so your result can change. You may get stuck on "people or alone" and "facts or ideas," and your answers can change depending on whether you picture a trip or a night alone watching movies.
ESFP>INFP.plus: You can't put your feelings into words because you feel so much. When you do find the words, they really reach people.
ESFP>INFP.tip: Try alternating "people days" and "alone days" in your schedule. You can slowly relive the fun from lively days on your quiet days, so tiredness won't pile up.
ESFP>INFP.hidden: When the season changes, you notice right away that the wind smells different. That's your temperament's way of enjoying the sights and sounds around you. Use it, and you can tell your friends all about the fun of a day out.

ESFP>ENFJ.title: Someone who wants to help as soon as they hear "I'd love to try that."
ESFP>ENFJ.body: When a junior coworker is working hard, you're the first to say "That's amazing!" Getting energy from people and deciding with feelings are the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament enjoys the moment and acts on the spot. Your character thinks about people's future and supports them with a plan.
ESFP>ENFJ.do: When a friend says they're moving, you pick a day to help on the spot and get others to come too.
ESFP>ENFJ.worry: Helping people makes you happy, so you can't say no, and your schedule fills up. The more you plan for everyone, the less time you have to just enjoy yourself.
ESFP>ENFJ.karai: Every reply you send comes with a sticker or emoji.
ESFP>ENFJ.aru: When a junior says "I'd like to try that someday," you say "Let's do it next month! I'll help," and set the date right there.
ESFP>ENFJ.why: By nature, you enjoy the fun in front of you and act on the spot. Along the way, you learned to think about people's future and support them with a plan. That's why, right in the middle of the excitement, you can plan out how to help.
ESFP>ENFJ.yure: Two things are different: "facts or ideas" and "plan or go with the flow." Answer as yourself cheering someone on, and you'll lean toward ideas and planning. Answer as yourself having fun, and you'll lean toward facts and going with the flow.
ESFP>ENFJ.plus: Your schedule fills up because when someone says, "I want to try this," you want to help right away. The people around you are really helped by how well you plan.
ESFP>ENFJ.tip: When you help with someone else's plans, put one of your own "I'd love to try" things on the calendar for the same month. Once it has a date, it won't stay at "someday."
ESFP>ENFJ.hidden: During a short break at work, do you enjoy your snack more than anyone? Your temperament knows how to enjoy the moment fully. Use it, and even on days your head is full of the future, you can get your energy back.

ESFP>ENFP.title: Someone who keeps coming up with fun ideas.
ESFP>ENFP.body: While eating cake at a café, you blurt out, "Want to open a shop together someday?" Getting energy from people, deciding with feelings, and going with the flow are the same in your temperament and your character. Only one thing is different: your temperament enjoys the fun right in front of you, and your character pictures things that don't exist yet.
ESFP>ENFP.do: When a friend invites you out on a day off, you'll change your plans to go.
ESFP>ENFP.worry: Fun things and things you want to try keep piling up, and you run out of time and energy. Picking just one is hard for you.
ESFP>ENFP.karai: At a friend's birthday party, you look like you're having more fun than the birthday person.
ESFP>ENFP.aru: You're talking with friends about "Where should we go next?" and the list of places gets so long you can't decide.
ESFP>ENFP.why: By nature, you enjoy the fun and feel of what's right in front of you. Along the way, you learned to get excited about things that don't exist yet. That's why a fun chat about now keeps growing into talk about the future.
ESFP>ENFP.yure: Answer while thinking about today's fun, and you'll lean toward facts. Answer while thinking about what you want to do next, and you'll lean toward ideas. Only one part is different, so you may go back and forth between two types.
ESFP>ENFP.plus: You can't pick just one because you find fun things now and in the future. Your cheerfulness makes people want to join in.
ESFP>ENFP.tip: In months with too much you want to do, decide "These three this month." If you're stuck, pick the one you'd do with someone, since a promise makes it easier to keep going.
ESFP>ENFP.hidden: When a friend's hair or clothes change a little, you're the first to say "That looks great." That's your temperament's way of really seeing the people in front of you. Use it, and people will be happy that you notice them.

ESFP>ISTJ.title: Someone who's careful at work and laughs a lot on breaks.
ESFP>ISTJ.body: When you hand off work, you do it carefully and end with a smile: "Just ask if you get stuck." Trusting facts and experience is the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament gets energy from people, decides with feelings, and acts on the spot. Your character likes calm time alone, decides with logic, and follows the steps.
ESFP>ISTJ.say: "I'll take care of it the usual way."
ESFP>ISTJ.do: You check your work papers several times before handing them in.
ESFP>ISTJ.worry: The more carefully you work, the more people rely on you, and the less time you get to just have fun. After choosing what's right, you wonder if you forgot about the other person's feelings.
ESFP>ISTJ.karai: Your work emails are stiff, but your texts to friends are full of stickers.
ESFP>ISTJ.aru: At work you're the "reliable one" with perfect paperwork, but on breaks you're the most excited one talking about the new bakery.
ESFP>ISTJ.why: By nature, you care about people's feelings and have fun acting on the spot. Along the way, you learned to prepare calmly and do things properly in order. That's why you're careful with work and warm with people.
ESFP>ISTJ.yure: Your result can change a lot depending on whether you answer as your work self or your day-off self. At work you'll lean toward alone, logic, and planning, and on days off, the opposite. The "facts" side stays the same either way.
ESFP>ISTJ.plus: If you feel you have less time for fun, it's because people trust you that much. Showing your fun side now and then softens the mood at work.
ESFP>ISTJ.tip: After deciding what's right, add "We were in a hurry so I went with this. What do you think?" Having one fun thing planned for the weekend helps you get through the week.
ESFP>ISTJ.hidden: Have you ever gone to a last-minute get-together and ended up having the most fun? Your temperament can enjoy things in the moment. Use it, and you won't panic when things don't go as planned.

ESFP>ISFJ.title: Someone who makes everyone laugh and brings a gift for each person.
ESFP>ISFJ.body: At a house party you're laughing the most, and when people leave, you hand everyone a little gift. Paying attention to the facts in front of you and deciding with feelings are the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament gets energy from people and enjoys the moment. Your character relaxes with time alone and prepares ahead.
ESFP>ISFJ.say: "I got juice too, for anyone who doesn't drink."
ESFP>ISFJ.do: When someone at work is out, you quietly help with their tasks.
ESFP>ISFJ.worry: You want to make people happy so much that you overdo the prep and you're exhausted on the day. After a fun time, you need quiet rest alone to get your energy back.
ESFP>ISFJ.karai: Even after hearing "That's plenty," you make one more dish.
ESFP>ISFJ.aru: When you visit a friend, you get their favorite snacks ready the day before. On the day, you come up with a new game on the spot and you're the most excited one.
ESFP>ISFJ.why: By nature, you get energy from people and go with the flow to have fun. Along the way, you learned to enjoy quiet time alone and prepare ahead. That's why you know right away what will make someone happy, and you enjoy both the prep and the day itself.
ESFP>ISFJ.yure: Two things are different: "people or alone" and "plan or go with the flow." Answer as yourself getting ready, and you'll lean toward alone and planning. Answer as yourself at the party, and you'll lean toward outgoing and going with the flow.
ESFP>ISFJ.plus: You put in effort before and on the day because you want to make people happy. The way you host stays in people's memories.
ESFP>ISFJ.tip: Stop your prep at "80% done by the night before." Leaving the rest for the day lets you relax and go along with whatever fun comes up.
ESFP>ISFJ.hidden: When the conversation stalls and it gets awkward, you can make everyone laugh with one casual line. That's your temperament's way of brightening a room. Show it more, and you'll be asked not just to support others but to lead too.

ESFP>ESTJ.title: Someone who organizes the event and still has the most fun.
ESFP>ESTJ.body: At the neighborhood cleanup, you quickly sort everyone into groups, and when it's done, you get a group photo. Getting energy from people and paying attention to the facts in front of you are the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament cares about people's feelings and has fun acting on the spot. Your character decides with logic and keeps things on schedule.
ESFP>ESTJ.do: Before a trip, you look up everyone's train times and send them out.
ESFP>ESTJ.worry: The more people say "You're so reliable," the less time you get to just have fun. Wanting to stick to the plan and wanting to enjoy the moment clash, so you get most tired on your days off.
ESFP>ESTJ.karai: You know everyone's schedule, but your own day off is never decided.
ESFP>ESTJ.aru: You set the restaurant and meeting time carefully, but on the night you're the one saying "Let's go to one more place!" and you stay till the end.
ESFP>ESTJ.why: By nature, you care about people's feelings and go with the flow to have fun. Along the way, you learned to decide with logic and follow the plan properly. That's why you're good at planning and good at having fun.
ESFP>ESTJ.yure: Two parts are different. You may get stuck on "logic or feelings" and "plan or go with the flow," so your result can change. Your answers depend on whether you picture yourself making plans or enjoying a detour.
ESFP>ESTJ.plus: You get most tired on days off because you think about everyone else first. On your days off, at least, it's fine not to make plans.
ESFP>ESTJ.tip: When you're organizing, leave one thing to "decide together on the day." If you leave a little open, you can keep to the plan and still enjoy the moment.
ESFP>ESTJ.hidden: Even when you have to point out a mistake, do you naturally pick words that won't bring the other person down? That's your temperament's way of thinking about people's feelings. Use it, and juniors will like you even when you have to be strict.

ESFP>ESFJ.title: Someone who often gets asked to plan celebrations.
ESFP>ESFJ.body: You handle the messages and the venue for the class reunion, and on the day you're the most excited one sharing old memories. Getting energy from people, looking at facts, and deciding with feelings are the same in your temperament and your character. Only one thing is different: your temperament enjoys the moment, and your character prepares ahead so no one has trouble.
ESFP>ESFJ.do: You give up your seat on the train and end up chatting happily with that person until your stop.
ESFP>ESFJ.worry: You set up rules so everyone can have fun, but on the day you want to just go with the mood. The harder you try to live up to expectations, the harder it is to say you're tired.
ESFP>ESFJ.karai: You tell people not to push themselves, but you rarely say it to yourself.
ESFP>ESFJ.aru: You had the flowers for the farewell party ready weeks ahead, but on the day you start crying before the guest of honor does.
ESFP>ESFJ.why: By nature, you like to go with the flow and have fun. Along the way, you learned to make plans and prepare properly. That's why you can prepare carefully and then enjoy the day just as you feel.
ESFP>ESFJ.yure: The only difference is "plan or go with the flow," so you may go back and forth between two types. Take it while preparing for an event, and you'll lean toward planning. Take it on a trip, and you'll lean toward going with the flow.
ESFP>ESFJ.plus: You can't say you're tired because you really want to live up to what people expect. The people who know you will gladly listen if you let a little of it out.
ESFP>ESFJ.tip: Ask someone to take just one part of the prep: "Could you handle this?" They'll be happy to help, so don't hold back.
ESFP>ESFJ.hidden: Even when your train is delayed on a trip, you can laugh and say "Let's walk around the station then." That's your temperament's way of enjoying surprises. You're usually busy preparing, so this hasn't come out much yet. Use it, and you can keep everyone cheerful even on days that don't go well.

ESFP>ISTP.title: Someone who's first to raise their hand for anything fun.
ESFP>ISTP.body: You're the first to jump in with "Ooh, that looks fun," and before long you're the one working most smoothly. Paying attention to what's in front of you and going with the flow are the same in your temperament and your character. Your temperament gets energy from people and cares about how others feel. Your character works quietly with your hands alone and decides simply with logic.
ESFP>ISTP.say: "Here, let me see. It's faster if you do it like this."
ESFP>ISTP.do: If a shelf at a friend's place is wobbly, you crack a joke and fix it in no time.
ESFP>ISTP.worry: Wanting to be gentle and wanting to be direct clash, so you're not sure how to say things. There's a big gap between days you want people around and days you want to be alone.
ESFP>ISTP.karai: When someone says "You can do everything!", you get shy and change the subject.
ESFP>ISTP.aru: You love having fun with people, but after three fun days in a row, a day comes when you don't want to answer anyone's messages.
ESFP>ISTP.why: By nature, you get energy from people and care about how others feel. Along the way, you learned to work quietly with your hands alone and decide clearly with logic. That's why working with you is fun, and people can count on you.
ESFP>ISTP.yure: If you answer as yourself fixing or making something, you'll lean toward alone and logic. Two parts are different, "people or alone" and "logic or feelings," so your result can change.
ESFP>ISTP.plus: Suddenly not wanting to talk to anyone means you can also recharge alone. After a rest, you're ready to go out and have fun again.
ESFP>ISTP.tip: If you're not sure how to say something, say your point briefly first, then add "But I get how you feel." On days you don't want to text, send one sticker that says "Taking a break today."
ESFP>ISTP.hidden: When a friend starts talking in a low voice, you ask "What's wrong?" before getting to anything else. That's your temperament's way of noticing feelings fast. Use it, and your help will fit what people really need.

ESFP>ISFP.title: Someone who's so happy to be invited that they overbook themselves.
ESFP>ISFP.body: On nice days, you head out even with no plans and stop by a favorite shop on the way home. Enjoying what's in front of you, deciding with feelings, and going with the flow are the same in your temperament and your character. Only where your energy comes from is different: your temperament gets energy from people, and your character recharges by doing what you love alone.
ESFP>ISFP.say: "I think I want to walk home alone, slowly."
ESFP>ISFP.do: When you find a song you love, you send it to your friends right away.
ESFP>ISFP.worry: You're so happy to be invited that you overbook, and later you run short on time for yourself. You work so hard to keep the mood bright that you miss the chance to talk about what you love.
ESFP>ISFP.karai: At a sale, you toss anything "so cute!" into your basket without checking the price.
ESFP>ISFP.aru: You turned down plans on Friday night and listened to your favorite music alone, and your energy came back.
ESFP>ISFP.why: By nature, you get energy from being with people. Along the way, you learned to recharge by doing what you love alone. That's why you can get energy from both lively time and quiet time.
ESFP>ISFP.yure: The only difference is "people or alone," so you may go back and forth between two types. Answer while thinking of a weekend out with friends, and you'll lean outgoing. Answer while thinking of a night alone with music, and you'll lean toward alone.
ESFP>ISFP.plus: You overbook because you truly enjoy time with people. Wanting time for yourself too means you're taking care of yourself.
ESFP>ISFP.tip: When you make plans, save one "night alone" each week first. If you missed the chance to talk about something you love, try sending "Actually..." later.
ESFP>ISFP.hidden: Your temperament knows how to spread fun with people. It shows when you take friends to a shop you love and everyone gets excited. Use it, and you'll find more and more friends who like the same things.

ESFP>ESTP.title: Someone who laughs off trouble and thinks of what's next.
ESFP>ESTP.body: The moment you find out the reservation didn't go through, you start looking for another place while making everyone laugh. Getting energy from people, enjoying the moment, and going with the flow are the same in your temperament and your character. Only one thing is different: your temperament decides with feelings, and your character weighs what's worth it and decides fast.
ESFP>ESTP.say: "That looks great on you! Why not wear it home?"
ESFP>ESTP.do: When your friend's train is late, you happily wait by browsing shops near the station.
ESFP>ESTP.worry: After deciding fast, you keep thinking back on how the other person felt. You often decide on impulse, so the small checks get pushed back.
ESFP>ESTP.karai: Before you know it, you've barely got any money left this month.
ESFP>ESTP.aru: When the fireworks show is rained out, you decide right away: "Let's do sparklers instead!" Back home, you think, "Maybe she really wanted to go."
ESFP>ESTP.why: By nature, you decide by caring about people's feelings. Along the way, you learned to decide quickly with logic. That's why you can decide fast when trouble hits, and still think about how others feel afterward.
ESFP>ESTP.yure: Answer while picturing trouble or money talk, and you'll lean toward logic. Answer while picturing memories with friends, and you'll lean toward feelings. The only difference is "logic or feelings," so you may go back and forth between two types.
ESFP>ESTP.plus: You keep thinking back because you're kind. Someone who can decide fast and still think of others is who people turn to when it matters.
ESFP>ESTP.tip: After deciding fast, ask "What does everyone think?" just once. For things you want to buy on impulse, leave them in your cart overnight, and you'll have fewer regrets.
ESFP>ESTP.hidden: When you pick a gift, do you get excited picturing their face as they open the box? That's your temperament's way of imagining people's happy faces. Use it at work too, and you'll think about "Will this make them happy?", and people will love it.

ESFP>ESFP.title: Someone who lights up the room.
ESFP>ESFP.body: Even at a party full of strangers, you end up laughing in the middle of the group. Your temperament and your character point the same way in all four directions, so your knack for enjoying the moment with people has grown straight and strong. You come alive in places with lots of connection, and you tend to lose energy in places where you work alone for a long time.
ESFP>ESFP.do: You've become good friends with the staff at the shops you go to often.
ESFP>ESFP.worry: While putting fun first, money and future plans get pushed back. When you're low on energy, it's often because you haven't been seeing people.
ESFP>ESFP.karai: The same night you decide "This month I'll save," you usually buy something.
ESFP>ESFP.aru: Even when you lose the shopping street raffle, you laugh "Too bad!" with a stranger standing there and somehow come home in a great mood.
ESFP>ESFP.why: By nature and now, you have fun with people, feel the joy in front of you, care about feelings, and act on the spot. That's why things that aren't about "right now," like money and future plans, tend to get pushed back.
ESFP>ESFP.yure: You'll likely get the same result every time. If a careful type or a type that likes being alone shows up, you may be seeing people less, or going along with others' pace a lot lately.
ESFP>ESFP.plus: You can't keep up with saving because you're great at noticing what makes you happy right now. That's also why you're the first to spot people's good sides and little joys.
ESFP>ESFP.tip: In your money app, set a "fun money" amount first, and spend freely within it. On low-energy days, send someone "Want to grab tea?" before trying to figure out why.
ESFP>ESFP.hidden: You're great at enjoying the moment, but you can also prepare steadily for the future. It shows when you save a little at a time for months for a trip you're excited about. Use it, and you can really get to the places you want to go.
